newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Litte excitement expected for Distrigas.
newsitem.headline: Litte excitement expected for Distrigas.

text.p: Belgian natural gas distributor Distrigas should show a modest rise in 1996 group net profit on Thursday but the acid test will come only in a few years time, analysts said.
"There is some risk (for Distrigas) because of the deregulation in the gas market," said Ruth Devenyns at KB Securities.
Analysts expected group net profit to rise to 1.35 billion francs on average from 1.27 billion in 1995. First-half group net profit edged up to 1.28 billion francs from 1.27 billion.
They also see a modest rise for 1997 and 1998 but the picture is less clear from 1999.

Distrigas, which is controlled by Belgian utility holding company Tractebel, said last September it expected full-year 1996 net profit and dividend on 1996 earnings to be at least equal to those of 1995.
It is expected to profit from transit contracts it signed to transport gas through the new Interconnector pipeline to the Belgian coast where it will enter the Distrigas system.
The 240-km (149 miles) Interconnector, the first gas pipeline to link Britain with continental Europe, is due to come on stream in October 1998.
"Transport (deals), rather than earnings will determine Distrigas's share price," said Sandra Vandermissen at G-Securities.

But analysts said Distrigas will also have to invest heavily into the improvement of its network to boost transit capacity from its Interconnector terminal. Distrigas plans to invest 12 to 15 billion francs ($343 to $429 million).
But Devenyns added however that the extra income from transport deals might not fully compensate for the loss of its distribution monopoly in a deregulated market.
Analysts said they were fairly positive for the share price of Distrigas, which was mainly attractive for its dividend yield -- currently at 4.6 percent.
But they noted that Distrigas has performed below par since its listing last June. It rose just six percent since the start of the year, compared with an overall bourse rise of some 13 percent.
Distrigas listed 16.6 percent of its capital last June at a fixed price of 28,000 francs.
On Monday it was quoted at 27,500 francs on the Brussels bourse, where it is subject to two daily price fixings, after having sunk to 25,000 francs last December from a high of 29,200 mid-June.

"It has gone up again, but compared to the bourse as a whole it's not very impressive," said Devenyns, who noted the bourse introduction price had been inflated by a bidding contest between Belgium's main banks.
She said that gas appeared more sensitive to deregulation than electricity but appeared to have a bigger growth potential.
"But it will never be a spectacular growth stock. It's not a high tech share," Devenyns said.
